title: Contact Structures On 5-Manifolds
notes: Open the lecture by naming the central upgrade from dimension three to dimension five. A contact form is still a maximally nonintegrable hyperplane field, but the topological bookkeeping now runs through almost-contact reductions, integral lifts of w2, and surgery. The dependency graph gives students a map before the theorem statements arrive.

title: The Existence Theorem
notes: Present the theorem as a topological gate plus a construction program. The obstruction W3 decides whether the five-manifold has almost-contact data at all, and the chapter's work shows that this data can be promoted to contact geometry in the simply connected setting. Stress that this is a paraphrase for lecture navigation, not a replacement for the source statement.

title: The Five-Dimensional Contact Test
notes: Use this slide to re-anchor the analytic definition. In dimension five, d alpha restricts to a symplectic form on a four-plane distribution, and the Reeb line supplies the missing direction. The wedge condition is not decoration: it is the local nondegeneracy test that every later surgery model must preserve near the handles.

title: The W3 Gate
notes: Pause on the warning because it prevents a common overstatement. A stable or formal-looking plane field is not enough; the tangent bundle must reduce from SO(5) to U(2) times a line. The obstruction is the integral Bockstein of w2, so the first question is whether w2 has an integral lift.

title: Bockstein Ladder
notes: Walk through the exact-sequence ladder slowly. Reduction mod two sends an integral class c to w2, and the Bockstein measures the failure of such a lift to exist. When beta of w2 vanishes, the possible lifts form an affine family shifted by twice integral cohomology classes, which foreshadows the c1 classification.

title: Almost-Contact Classes By c1
notes: Here the classification becomes usable. On the simply connected five-manifolds in this chapter, the homotopy class of the almost-contact reduction is recorded by c1 with the single parity requirement that c1 reduce to w2. The visual lattice is meant to show that changing c1 by two times a class keeps the same mod-two shadow.

title: Why F5 Is Manageable
notes: Explain why obstruction theory does not explode in dimension five. The fiber SO(5) over U(2) is CP3, equivalently SO(6) over U(3). Up to the dimension of the manifold, its relevant homotopy is concentrated in degree two, so the obstruction-theory story collapses to a first Chern class calculation.

title: Stable Twist Formula
notes: Use the formula as the algebraic hinge between formal data and surgery choices. Once a base stable complex structure is chosen, twisting by u changes c1 by twice u. That factor of two is the same parity phenomenon from the Bockstein ladder, and it will reappear when a framing integer is read by contact surgery.

title: Two S3-Bundles Over S2
notes: This slide turns a classification fact into a memory device. There are two oriented S3-bundles over S2 in the simply connected list: the product and the twisted bundle. They have the same visible base-and-fiber shape, so the distinguishing datum is a parity signal carried by the framing or by the associated w2 behavior.

title: Barden Pieces In The Chapter
notes: Give students the large-scale decomposition before discussing individual constructions. A simply connected five-manifold with W3 equal to zero has two cases: if w2 vanishes, the free part is copies of S2 times S3; if w2 is nonzero, one free summand is replaced by X_infty. The torsion block M_t has H2 equal to G, w2 zero, and is obtained smoothly from S5 by surgery on a link of two-spheres.

title: Surgery Roadmap
notes: Describe surgery as the construction engine. The topological handle changes the five-manifold while the contact framing keeps the boundary geometry under control. In the free-generator move, the handle can create or cancel the appropriate H2 contribution, and the chosen integer controls the resulting Euler-class or c1 bookkeeping.

title: Torsion Blocks M_t
notes: For torsion pieces, the student should track the finite second-homology block rather than a tunable c1 ledger. In the chapter's M_t blocks, H squared is zero, so each orientation has only one almost-contact homotopy class. The construction realizes the block by contact surgery along Legendrian two-spheres.

title: The X_infty Framing Route
notes: The twisted S3-bundle is produced by the same standard isotropic circle surgery mechanism as the product case, but with odd framing parity. The framing integer lives in pi one of U one, maps mod two to the smooth bundle type, and still records the contact c one data.

title: Contact Existence For M_t
notes: Now return from the free-bundle framing story to the torsion family. Since H squared of M_t is zero, there is no c one choice to tune; the proof only has to produce a contact structure on the torsion block. Emphasize that the surgery data is used to realize M_t itself, not to select among multiple almost-contact homotopy classes.

title: Framing Parity Lab
notes: Make the integer framing feel concrete. The framing group pi1 of U(1) is Z, so rotating once changes an integer, but the bundle type only sees its parity while c1 changes by even increments. This is the short laboratory calculation that explains why even and odd framings route to the two S3-bundles over S2.

title: Recap And Exercise
notes: Close by asking students to run the whole chapter pipeline on a hypothetical simply connected five-manifold. First test W3, then choose an integral lift c of w2, then read the Barden decomposition, and finally decide which surgery blocks and framing parity are needed. The exercise is intentionally synthetic because the chapter's main skill is coordinated bookkeeping.
